online_work_scope.note: setup() fixes shard_size_bytes = ring_dim * record_bytes = 2048 records, independent of N. The online answer therefore touches one 2048-record shard no matter how large the database is, and ClientQuery.shard_id is sent in cleartext, so the server learns which shard the query is in. The anonymity set is 2048 records, not N.

notes: Measured on ryzen9900x-8t-32g. security_bits=128 is claimed by the implementation and is published as a label only — it is not verified here. Scheme params are whatever this implementation chose; compare across implementations with that in mind. CAVEAT: Upstream 0.2.0's query() calls maybe_generate_packing_keys() on EVERY query — there is no session or key-cache API. Raven's fork added pir/session.rs (ClientSession + a packing-key pre-exchange handshake, keys uploaded once and referenced by handle). So client_query_gen_ms and query_bytes for this row include per-query InspiRING key generation and shipping, while inspire-raven's do not. That is a real difference between the implementations, not a harness artifact — but the two per-query numbers are not measuring the same work, and any comparison must say so. CODE PATH: in this codebase respond_with_variant() dispatches OnePacking and TwoPacking to the same function (respond_inspiring), so requesting TwoPacking actually runs InsPIRe^1, not InsPIRe^2. Raven's fork patched this exact fall-through. The row is therefore not executing the same algorithm as inspire-raven's TwoPacking row even though both are labelled two-packing. CAVEAT: Run with 1 seed x 4 measured iterations instead of the 3 x 16 used for inspire-raven. This implementation's per-query cost is ~2000x higher (4.0 s vs 1.9 ms at 2^20 x 8 B on the reference machine), so the default counts are unfinishable at the larger cells. Fewer iterations lowers confidence in the number; it does not change what is being measured. The counts actually used are recorded in params.scheme_params. The pre-fork baseline. github.com/igor53627/inspire-rs — the upstream that inspire-raven and inspire-lianghuiqiang9 both descend from — has been DELETED from GitHub; crates.io inspire 0.2.0 (published 2026-02-15) is the only surviving copy. Its secure_128_d2048 uses the 2-CRT moduli [268369921, 249561089] (q ~ 2^56), which is exactly the parameter set Raven's fork replaced with a single-prime q = 2^60 - 2^14 + 1, calling it under-provisioned. Benchmarked through a driver crate in this repo, since the published crate ships no BenchReport emitter.
